record.original_question: If f is univalent analytic in D, then it is well known (see Pommerenke [656, p. 262]) that both f and its first derivative f ′ must be normal, while R z the higher derivatives f (n) need not be normal if n ≥ 2. Setting f (−1) (z) = 0 f (t) dt and Rz f (−n−1) (z) = 0 f (−n) (t) dt, it is easy to verify that f (−2) is Bloch; while if n ≥ 3, f (−n) is bounded (hence Bloch, and therefore normal). Thus, if f is univalent analytic in D, then the functions f (n) must be normalR for n = 1, 0, −2, −3, . . . , and need not z be normal for n = 2, 3, . . .. Must f (−1) (z) = 0 f (t) dt be normal if f (z) is univalent analytic in D? (D. Campbell)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk. A meromorphic function $g$ on $D$ is called normal if the family $\{g\circ\varphi:\varphi\in\operatorname{Aut}(D)\}$ is a normal family in the sense of Montel, equivalently if \[\sup_{z\in D}(1-|z|^2)\,\frac{|g'(z)|}{1+|g(z)|^2}<\infty.\] For an analytic function $f:D\to\mathbb{C}$, define its iterated antiderivatives by \[f^{(-1)}(z)=\int_0^z f(t)\,dt,\qquad f^{(-n-1)}(z)=\int_0^z f^{(-n)}(t)\,dt\quad(n\ge1).\]

It is known that if $f$ is univalent and analytic in $D$, then both $f$ and $f'$ are normal, while $f^{(n)}$ need not be normal for $n\ge2$; moreover $f^{(-2)}$ is a Bloch function and $f^{(-n)}$ is bounded (hence normal) for every $n\ge3$.

Question: If $f$ is univalent and analytic in $D$, must the antiderivative \[f^{(-1)}(z)=\int_0^z f(t)\,dt\] be a normal function on $D$?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published resolution of this question (whether the antiderivative of every univalent analytic function on the unit disk is normal). Related work on univalent Bloch functions and Pommerenke's results appears, but no source confirming a positive or negative answer to the specific question was located, so the status is recorded as unknown.

status_evidence.title: On univalent Bloch functions
status_evidence.snippet: Study of Bloch property for univalent functions, building on Pommerenke's results.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature exists on univalent functions and the Bloch/normal property, but does not directly resolve the antiderivative question.

status_evidence.title: On univalent functions, Bloch functions and VMOA
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses connections between univalent functions, Bloch functions, and VMOA.
status_evidence.claim: No explicit resolution of the normality of the antiderivative of a univalent function was found.
